corrections.comment:
Checked the factual claims against the fixtures and the scenario. Diocese of
Scranton 1868 is grounded -- loc_001 carries both the diocese and the date.
Schuylkill County 1811 from Berks and Northampton, and PA statewide civil
registration from 1906, are not in any fixture but are historically correct, so
they are model knowledge rather than fabrication. Ten items, all record types
present in the collections_search and volume_search responses. Nothing cites an
identifier the run was not served.

First plan for q_001 with nothing to supersede, 10 items, fallbacks encoded, and
the name-variant point is real rather than asserted -- "Sheehan" appears 5 times
in what was written alongside "Sheahan", and "variant" 5 times. Request was for
a first plan and a first plan is what it produced.

Seven calls, all matched a fixture, none returned fixture_not_found. One
correction to the judge's wording: place_search was called with
placeName="Schuylkill County" plus contextName="Pennsylvania", not "Schuylkill"
-- it still matches the fixture predicate, so the score is right and only the
description is loose. collections_search, volume_search and
external_links_search all used standardPlace "Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, United
States" with 1870-1910.

Every rationale ties back to Michael Sheahan's relocation or employment. No item
chases a relative's record as an end in itself.

Verified all three fallback chains against the data, not the prose: seq 3
fallback_for pli_002, seq 5 fallback_for pli_004, seq 8 fallback_for pli_007.
Free and indexed sources lead, paid and browse-only follow. Worth noting given
007 in the last run scored 3 with nine null fallback_for fields -- here the field
is genuinely populated.

Schuylkill County 1811-present, Diocese of Scranton from 1868 per loc_001, US
ports appropriate for Irish arrivals 1870-1895. No pre-1811 parent county is
searched for post-1811 records, which is the error this dimension exists to
catch.

Confirmed from the response rather than the judge's summary: research_query
returned {"ok": true, "section": "plans", "count": 0, "items": []}, so there was
genuinely no prior plan. One research_append with 11 ops -- one plan at status
"active" plus 10 items. No prior plan's status touched, because none existed.

judge_context[2] says do NOT penalize the plan for the Wood-census item's
rationale not repeating the caveat, as long as the caveat appears somewhere in
the plan. It does: "Assertion a_003 explicitly flags that 'Wood' is unconfirmed
as a birth surname." The judge admits the caution section exists, then marks it
down anyway. No false statement is identified, and no validator failed.

Ten items; judge_context[0]'s direct-parentage requirement met by pli_002,
pli_003, pli_007, pli_008.

Types match the information need. pli_010 as `other` is right — church, cemetery
and local history have no recommended enum value.

pli_009 corroborates the parents' identity rather than chasing siblings for
their own sake.

Checked the fields, not the prose: pli_003 fallback_for pli_002, pli_006
fallback_for pli_005. Free and indexed lead.
Smith County TX for 1869–70, Blount County AL for 1840–80. Nothing anachronistic.
First plan for q_002, created active, one research_append, no prior plan touched.

Checked the collection ids against the responses. 1999196 is cited as "indexed,
~893K records" and the run's collections_search hit standardPlace="Pennsylvania,
United States", whose fixture serves that collection with personCount=893214. So
the claim matches a response it actually received, and the availability validator
correctly passed.

Worth recording: the same collection is served with personCount=0 by
collections-search-schuylkill.json. That inconsistency between two fixtures is
why 006 fails this dimension's validator and q7m doesn't — it depends only on
which place the skill searched.

Nine items, and every required field present on all nine — checked sequence,
record_type, jurisdiction, date_range, repository, rationale, fallback_for,
status. research_query returned count: 0, so first-plan was correct. Execution
continued as authorized: skills_invoked = ['research-plan', 'search-records',
'search-external-sites'].

Five calls, zero fixture_not_found. collections_search and external_links_search
both used standardPlace="Pennsylvania, United States" with 1838-1910.
Types match the information need, and each rationale names what the type yields.

The FAN items state what they reveal about the Doyle children rather than
pursuing Ellen or Bridget for their own sake.

One fallback chain, on item 8, and fallback_for is genuinely populated rather
than described in prose only. Free and indexed lead, external last.

Schuylkill County correct for 1838-1968; pre-1906 births routed to church
records, which is the right consequence of no civil registration.

research_query returned {"count": 0, "items": []}, so nothing to supersede. One
plan created active for q_001.

Checked every identifier against the declared fixtures, not the judge's summary:
1417491 / 1804888 / 1875188 in collections-search-kentucky, 007991103 / 007834412
in volume-search-muhlenberg, Ancestry 1222 in external-links-search-kentucky. All
six are grounded. Note the run log alone cannot show this — fixture-served calls
persist response=None and record only the fixture name, so verification means
reading the fixture files.

Six items, all status "planned". Probate (pli_005) present, which is this test's
requirement, and the era mismatch is flagged — certificates begin 1911, subject
last documented 1870.
Seven calls, no fixture_not_found, every call matched a declared fixture.

Four vital_record, one probate, one cemetery. Probate as the pre-1911 alternative
is the point of the scenario and it is there.
All six items target Elijah Wilkins. No FAN items, so no scope question arises.

Checked the fields: seq 3 and seq 4 both fallback_for pli_002 — two independent
fallbacks on one item, which is correct here (browse-only images and a paid index
are alternatives to each other). Indexed before unindexed, free before paid.

Both dates are grounded: 1792 in place-search-kentucky-catchall, 1798 in
place-search-muhlenberg. Correct for an 1870s–90s death.

First plan for q_001, one plan active, six items planned, nothing pre-existing
touched. test_research_plan_new_plan_for_q_001 passed — this is the test that had
been failing since 2026-08-24, and it passes on its own merits.

The supersede is real, not described: research_append{section: "plans", op:
"update", entryId: "pl_002", fields: {status: "superseded"}} returned ok with
research.json written. Then a second call appended pl_003 active plus five items.
test_pli_006_status_unchanged passed, so the in-progress item was left intact.

Five items, all status "planned", full metadata. Audit trail preserved —
plans_no_deletions, no_entries_deleted and log_append_only all passed.

collections_search used standardPlace "Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, United States"
with 1860-1870, matching the corrected window. No fixture_not_found. One
correction to the judge's wording: this was two research_append calls, not a
single batch — an update for pl_002 then an append for pl_003. That is the right
shape, since a status change and a new plan are different operations.

Probate, church burial, two military, one marriage. Church burial as the primary
1865 death record is right given no PA civil registration until 1906.

Thomas's and Mary's records are pursued for what they say about Patrick's
parentage, not for their own sake.

Checked the field: seq 4 carries fallback_for pli_009. Free and indexed before
the paid Ancestry fallback.

County-level for probate and church, state-level for Civil War regiments. The
1906 death and 1885 marriage registration dates are both correct for
Pennsylvania and are what justify the church searches.

Supersede mode was correct: pl_002 was active with pli_006 targeting 1870-1890,
invalidated by the ~1865 death reference. pl_002 set superseded before pl_003
was created, exactly one plan now active, prior items untouched.

The arguments were correct; the fixture is missing. contextName is a declared
parameter (place-search.ts:41), and the second call used the exact shape that
succeeded twice in this run ("Blount County, Alabama", "Smith County, Texas").
No place-search Georgia fixture exists, though the test declares
collections-search-georgia. That is a corpus gap being charged to the model.

Retracting this. I claimed `naturalization` was a recommended record_type — it
is not. The recommended list is census, vital_record, probate, land, church,
military, newspaper, cemetery, tax, immigration, court, other. "Naturalization"
is in the fact-type enum; my check was a substring match over the whole file and
hit an unrelated key. @T-FEH caught it.

So pli_006 used a recommended value. `court` is arguable, but that is a choice
between two recommended values, not a partial failure. Agreeing at 3.

The judge did describe the item as "Naturalization (pli_006)" while the field
reads `immigration` — grading the rationale, not the field, same as 007 last
round. Worth watching, not a score cut.
